cases.class: other (operand restriction: 2023 SR6 bans an ACTIVE-CLASS returning item for a get property method; 2002 SR6 has no such ban, so the 2002 rule governs get property methods 2023 cannot have)
cases.reason: The format and GR6 are word-identical, but the set of methods GR6 makes get property methods is larger in 2002. 2002 SR6 asks only for no USING parameters and a single RETURNING item. 2023 SR6 adds 'The returning item shall not be an object reference described with the ACTIVE-CLASS phrase' (a 2014 addition). 2002 lets ACTIVE-CLASS stand in a method's linkage section (13.16.58.2 SR15), and the 2002 object-property clause (8.4.2.9) has no ACTIVE-CLASS ban. So METHOD-ID. GET PROPERTY P. with PROCEDURE DIVISION RETURNING LK-R, LK-R USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE ACTIVE-CLASS, is legal 2002 and GR6 makes it the get property method for P. The 2023 row never sees that method. The reader called SR6 'a separate syntax rule', but it decides which methods GR6 reaches. Compiler at 2002: WRONG. Probe prop_active_class.cob at --std 2002 gives error COBOL2790 'the returning item of a get property method shall not be an object reference described with the ACTIVE-CLASS phrase (ISO §2023:11.7.3 SR6)': the 2023 ban is applied at 2002. Expected at 2002: compiles. Needs a defect note (gate COBOL2790 to 2014+) and then a 2002 witness.
